{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the increment within the existing Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring Cloud Data Flow-style module boundaries rather than introducing a new platform architecture.",
    "Represent composed-job progress as the aggregate of child-job progress, with defined handling for queued, running, completed, failed, and skipped child jobs.",
    "Implement composed-job restart through an explicit restart operation that reuses the existing job definition and execution metadata while preventing accidental duplicate active executions.",
    "Treat the Kafka 0.9 work as an integration investigation and compatibility prototype, including documented findings and recommended changes rather than a complete Kafka subsystem rewrite.",
    "Treat Lattice bare-metal support as a bootstrap proof of concept with repeatable provisioning scripts and documented prerequisites, not as a production-grade infrastructure product.",
    "Resolve dot-delimited Tuple and JSON properties through the existing stream-definition parser and property-resolution mechanisms, preserving backward compatibility with existing syntax.",
    "Implement shell tab completion using the shell framework's command metadata and option descriptors, with completion for supported commands, modules, and known option values.",
    "Implement Mesos deployment through an adapter or deployer integration that maps application launch, scaling, environment, health, and shutdown operations to Mesos primitives.",
    "Move Redis test rules and fixtures into a separately buildable repository or module, publish a versioned artifact, and update consumers to use that artifact.",
    "Use automated unit and integration tests as the primary verification mechanism, with targeted manual validation for Kafka, Lattice, shell completion, and Mesos environments."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing source repositories, build system, CI configuration, and development environments are available and build successfully before the increment begins.",
    "The estimates represent one developer's hands-on work-hours, including implementation, test development, debugging, documentation, and local validation; elapsed calendar time is excluded.",
    "Existing APIs and conventions are preferred, and no major incompatible public API redesign is required.",
    "The specification does not identify exact versions of Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, the shell framework, Mesos, Lattice, or the Kafka client; compatible versions will be selected based on the existing project baseline.",
    "Kafka 0.9 investigation requires a working compatibility test and a written recommendation, but does not require production rollout or migration of all supported Kafka deployments.",
    "Lattice and Mesos validation environments can be accessed locally or through an existing test environment; provisioning physical hardware, network infrastructure, or cloud accounts is excluded.",
    "The Mesos work covers a functional initial deployer integration and representative deployment scenarios, not exhaustive support for every Mesos scheduler, framework, or operating-system combination.",
    "Redis test-rule extraction does not require changing the behavior of the Redis production integration; it requires repository/module separation, packaging, consumer migration, and regression tests.",
    "Documentation is limited to developer and user documentation needed to operate and maintain the delivered features.",
    "Code review by other people, release management, long-term maintenance, and post-release support are excluded."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment setup and baseline analysis",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing repositories and architecture, identify affected modules and extension points, establish the local build and test baseline, and refine the implementation plan for all eight user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Aggregated progress for composed jobs",
      "activity_description": "Define composed-job progress semantics, implement aggregation of child-job execution states and progress, expose the result through the existing job status model or endpoint, and add unit and integration tests for normal, partial, failed, and completed executions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 60
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Restart support for composed jobs",
      "activity_description": "Implement the composed-job restart command/service, validate restart eligibility, recreate or relaunch the composed execution using existing definitions, handle duplicate and failed child executions, and add persistence, API, and end-to-end tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Kafka 0.9 integration investigation",
      "activity_description": "Review Kafka 0.9 protocol and client compatibility, create a focused integration prototype against the existing stream or messaging components, identify incompatibilities and improvement opportunities, run representative tests, and document findings and recommendations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Lattice bare-metal bootstrap investigation",
      "activity_description": "Evaluate Lattice deployment and bootstrap options for s-c-d bare-metal infrastructure, create a repeatable proof-of-concept setup or provisioning scripts, validate service startup and connectivity, and document prerequisites, limitations, and recommended architecture.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Dot-delimited Tuple and JSON property resolution",
      "activity_description": "Extend stream-definition parsing and property binding to support dot-delimited properties for Tuple and JSON payloads, preserve existing property formats, handle nested and missing values, and add parser, binding, and runtime integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Shell tab completion",
      "activity_description": "Add command, module, option, and applicable value completion to the s-c-d shell, integrate completion metadata with command registration, handle incomplete and ambiguous input, and add automated shell-level tests plus usage documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Mesos deployment support",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement the Mesos deployment integration, map application lifecycle and scaling operations to Mesos resources and tasks, support configuration and environment propagation, implement health and shutdown behavior, and validate representative deployment and failure scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Redis test-rule repository extraction",
      "activity_description": "Extract Redis Rule implementations and supporting fixtures into a separate buildable repository or module, define packaging and versioning, update existing consumers and build files, and add regression coverage to verify fixture behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature regression, documentation, and delivery hardening",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and regression suite, resolve cross-module defects, perform compatibility checks, update user and developer documentation, clean up configuration and examples, and prepare the increment for CI and release consumption.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 400
  }
}

I’m assuming that the existing legacy code remains compatible with the Spring version, but what about Java 17? The specification indicates it's general, but I’m thinking it may relate to Spring XD. I should probably maintain existing project APIs and the test stack. Targeting Java 17 compatibility seems risky, only if absolutely necessary. I'll also keep my estimates as work hours, and validate the JSON.

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment within the existing Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring Cloud Data Flow-style module boundaries rather than introducing a new platform architecture.
Represent composed-job progress as the aggregate of child-job progress, with defined handling for queued, running, completed, failed, and skipped child jobs.
Implement composed-job restart through an explicit restart operation that reuses the existing job definition and execution metadata while preventing accidental duplicate active executions.
Treat the Kafka 0.9 work as an integration investigation and compatibility prototype, including documented findings and recommended changes rather than a complete Kafka subsystem rewrite.
Treat Lattice bare-metal support as a bootstrap proof of concept with repeatable provisioning scripts and documented prerequisites, not as a production-grade infrastructure product.
Resolve dot-delimited Tuple and JSON properties through the existing stream-definition parser and property-resolution mechanisms, preserving backward compatibility with existing syntax.
Implement shell tab completion using the shell framework's command metadata and option descriptors, with completion for supported commands, modules, and known option values.
Implement Mesos deployment through an adapter or deployer integration that maps application launch, scaling, environment, health, and shutdown operations to Mesos primitives.
Move Redis test rules and fixtures into a separately buildable repository or module, publish a versioned artifact, and update consumers to use that artifact.
Use automated unit and integration tests as the primary verification mechanism, with targeted manual validation for Kafka, Lattice, shell completion, and Mesos environments.
assumptions: The existing source repositories, build system, CI configuration, and development environments are available and build successfully before the increment begins.
The estimates represent one developer's hands-on work-hours, including implementation, test development, debugging, documentation, and local validation; elapsed calendar time is excluded.
Existing APIs and conventions are preferred, and no major incompatible public API redesign is required.

The specification does not identify exact versions of Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, the shell framework, Mesos, Lattice, or the Kafka client; compatible versions will be selected based on the existing project baseline.
Kafka 0.9 investigation requires a working compatibility test and a written recommendation, but does not require production rollout or migration of all supported Kafka deployments.
Lattice and Mesos validation environments can be accessed locally or through an existing test environment; provisioning physical hardware, network infrastructure, or cloud accounts is excluded.
The Mesos work covers a functional initial deployer integration and representative deployment scenarios, not exhaustive support for every Mesos scheduler, framework, or operating-system combination.
Redis test-rule extraction does not require changing the behavior of the Redis production integration; it requires repository/module separation, packaging, consumer migration, and regression tests.
Documentation is limited to developer and user documentation needed to operate and maintain the delivered features.
Code review by other people, release management, long-term maintenance, and post-release support are excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing repositories and architecture, identify affected modules and extension points, establish the local build and test baseline, and refine the implementation plan for all eight user stories.

Define composed-job progress semantics, implement aggregation of child-job execution states and progress, expose the result through the existing job status model or endpoint, and add unit and integration tests for normal, partial, failed, and completed executions.

Implement the composed-job restart command/service, validate restart eligibility, recreate or relaunch the composed execution using existing definitions, handle duplicate and failed child executions, and add persistence, API, and end-to-end tests.

Review Kafka 0.9 protocol and client compatibility, create a focused integration prototype against the existing stream or messaging components, identify incompatibilities and improvement opportunities, run representative tests, and document findings and recommendations.

Evaluate Lattice deployment and bootstrap options for s-c-d bare-metal infrastructure, create a repeatable proof-of-concept setup or provisioning scripts, validate service startup and connectivity, and document prerequisites, limitations, and recommended architecture.

activities.activity_description: Extend stream-definition parsing and property binding to support dot-delimited properties for Tuple and JSON payloads, preserve existing property formats, handle nested and missing values, and add parser, binding, and runtime integration tests.

Add command, module, option, and applicable value completion to the s-c-d shell, integrate completion metadata with command registration, handle incomplete and ambiguous input, and add automated shell-level tests plus usage documentation.

Design and implement the Mesos deployment integration, map application lifecycle and scaling operations to Mesos resources and tasks, support configuration and environment propagation, implement health and shutdown behavior, and validate representative deployment and failure scenarios.

Extract Redis Rule implementations and supporting fixtures into a separate buildable repository or module, define packaging and versioning, update existing consumers and build files, and add regression coverage to verify fixture behavior.
